before: Chromosomes were unknown in 1834 when Gregor Mendel proposed his classic concept of heredity. In the late 1880s, scientists finally could stain cell structures with the clarity to identify chromosomes. Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri, in 1902 and 1903 respectively, independently published papers suggesting that genes—which determine the physical characteristics of offspring—were located within chromosomes, a concept later referred to as the "chromosome theory of inheritance." Prior to Sutton's and Boveri's research, the scientific community was relatively undecided on where genes reside. Thomas Hunt Morgan was originally skeptical of the Sutton–Boveri chromosome theory of inheritance. However, he noticed some unusual trends while conducting experiments on fruit flies. Through observing the fruit flies' eye color over countless generations, he eventually concluded that the eye color gene is passed down through the X chromosome, not the Y chromosome, meaning that eye color is connected to sex chromosomes. Morgan later won the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discovery.
after:
Text 1

Chromosomes were unknown in 1834 when Gregor Mendel proposed his classic concept of heredity. In the late 1880s, scientists finally could stain cell structures with the clarity to identify chromosomes. Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri, in 1902 and 1903 respectively, independently published papers suggesting that genes—which determine the physical characteristics of offspring—were located within chromosomes, a concept later referred to as the "chromosome theory of inheritance." Prior to Sutton's and Boveri's research, the scientific community was relatively undecided on where genes reside.

Text 2

Thomas Hunt Morgan was originally skeptical of the Sutton–Boveri chromosome theory of inheritance. However, he noticed some unusual trends while conducting experiments on fruit flies. Through observing the fruit flies' eye color over countless generations, he eventually concluded that the eye color gene is passed down through the X chromosome, not the Y chromosome, meaning that eye color is connected to sex chromosomes. Morgan later won the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discovery.
